query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The concurrent improvement of strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys can be achieved through the homogeneous distribution of precipitates within grains, rather than at grain boundaries, which prevents intergranular embrittlement and allows for high ductility.
generation.intervention: Homogeneous distribution of precipitates within grains
generation.conditions: Annealing at 900 °C for 5 min followed by aging at 650 °C for 20 h; room temperature tensile testing
generation.mechanism: Prevention of intergranular embrittlement and promotion of high ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Concurrent improvement of strength and ductility
generation.baseline: Traditional alloys with precipitates at grain boundaries
generation.uncertainty: The mechanism may not apply to all high-entropy alloys or processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of high-entropy alloys with homogeneous and heterogeneous distributions of precipitates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the homogeneous distribution of precipitates does not lead to concurrent improvement of strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified

Mechanism: Coherent interfaces of nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preventing premature crack initiation and maintaining ductility while providing strength.. System: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (at.%) refractory high-entropy alloy with stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs). Conditions: Ambient temperature and 800 °C; tensile deformation up to 14% strain; after stepwise thermo-mechanical processing (cold rolling, annealing at 900 °C, aging at 650 °C). Evidence: measured. Observation: Dislocations cut through δ-lamellae and are pinned by γ″ particles; shearing of δ-lamellae leads to coherent misalignment rather than microcrack formation at 14% strain.. Scope limits: Does not hold for traditional alloys with brittle secondary phases (e.g., silicides, B2, Laves) or intermetallic compounds at grain boundaries which cause embrittlement.. Alternatives: Single precipitation processes (limited strengthening potency) and non-coherent precipitates (cause brittle fracture).. Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Homogeneous distribution of precipitates within grains (rather than at boundaries) prevents intergranular embrittlement and allows for high ductility.. System: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy with δ-lamellae and γ″ particles. Conditions: Annealing at 900 °C for 5 min followed by aging at 650 °C for 20 h; room temperature tensile testing.. Evidence: measured. Observation: δ-lamellae nucleated at dislocation pile-ups via rapid pipe diffusion, resulting in homogeneous distribution within fcc grains.. Scope limits: Specific to the stepwise thermo-mechanical processing used; not tested for other processing routes.. Alternatives: Precipitation at grain boundaries which leads to intergranular embrittlement in traditional alloys.. Quote: "This effect results in the homogeneous distribution of δ-lamellae within the fcc grains, instead of precipitation at grain boundaries that can lead to intergranular embrittlement in traditional alloys."
